expectations.text: Identifies Article 22 GDPR: solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects (such as account deactivation affecting livelihood) are prohibited unless an exception applies, and safeguards are required
expectations.evidence: Quotes Art. 22(1); "Deactivating a driver's account is a textbook example of a decision with legal or similarly significant effect"; Art. 22(2) exceptions and 22(3) safeguards covered

expectations.text: Cites the August 2026 enforcement precedent: the Dutch DPA (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) fined Uber approximately €825 million (€824,990,000) for fully automated driver-account deactivations without human assessment — the second-largest GDPR fine ever
expectations.evidence: Omits the August 2026 Dutch AP €824,990,000 Uber fine; cites only older SCHUFA/Ola/Amsterdam Court of Appeal matters

expectations.text: Requires meaningful human review before deactivation decisions take effect — a human who can influence the outcome, not a rubber-stamp of the model output
expectations.evidence: "If a human merely rubber-stamps the model's output... regulators will still treat this as solely automated. The human involvement has to be meaningful"

expectations.text: Identifies the transparency duty: drivers must be informed about the existence and logic of the automated decision-making and its consequences (Arts. 13/14/15(1)(h))
expectations.evidence: "Articles 13(2)(f) and 14(2)(g) require you to give data subjects meaningful information about the logic involved, the significance, and the envisaged consequences"

expectations.text: Mentions the data subject's right to contest the decision, obtain human intervention, and express their point of view (Art. 22(3))
expectations.evidence: "Article 22(3) requires... the right to obtain human intervention, to express their point of view, and to contest the decision"
